key_insight: HiAR prevents progressive quality degradation in autoregressive long-video diffusion by preserving calibrated uncertainty in context through hierarchical denoising, enabling temporally continuous generation over long horizons.
problem_solved: Reduces error accumulation and loss of temporal continuity in autoregressive (AR) diffusion video generation, which otherwise degrades quality as generation proceeds.
method: Hierarchical denoising: condition generation on multi-level (noisy → clean) context representations to avoid overconfident propagation of past prediction errors.
Autoregressive long-video pipeline: generate video segments sequentially while exchanging hierarchical context to maintain temporal consistency across long horizons.
Efficiency-oriented design: structured conditioning and denoising schedule that balances sampling cost with robustness to accumulated errors.
impact: Enables more stable, longer-duration video synthesis with diffusion-based AR models, making generative video systems more practical for long-form content, simulations, and downstream tasks that require temporal coherence.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing autoregressive segment generation with hierarchical denoising levels (noisy → intermediate → clean) passed as context between segments.
Line chart comparing quality vs. generated length: baseline AR diffusion dropping over time vs. HiAR maintaining higher quality.
Timeline/frame-strip demonstrating a long generated video with consistent appearance and motion across segments.
Schematic illustrating how preserving uncertainty in context prevents confident error propagation (iconography for noise, uncertainty, and corrected predictions).
paper_title: HiAR: Efficient Autoregressive Long Video Generation via Hierarchical Denoising
paper_authors: Kai Zou, Dian Zheng, Hongbo Liu, Tiankai Hang, Bin Liu
